summary: Richard B. Martin worked in Tibetology and Indology at the University of Virginia, serving as Professor (attested 1983–1991) and as South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker studied at Wisconsin-Madison, Minnesota, Colorado Boulder, Harvard, and UC Berkeley, and with Shunryu Suzuki. Active in Buddhist and religious studies, he founded and led the San Francisco Zen Center and held posts at Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Iowa.

Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Historian and Indologist Richard Bertram Whitehead studied at Liverpool College, Exeter College, Oxford, and Cambridge. He co-founded the Numismatic Society of India in 1910 and became Fellow-Commoner and Advisor to Indian students at St John's College in 1922.

Richard Bowring, a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned degrees from Cambridge. He held fellowships in Japan, taught at Columbia and Princeton, and served at Cambridge as Professor from 1985 and Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

Richard Burghart, who worked in Indology and religious studies, earned degrees from Williams College and SOAS. He taught Asian anthropology at the London School of Economics and SOAS before becoming Professor of Anthropology at Heidelberg University in 1988.

Richard Burn was an Indologist and historian who studied at Christ Church, Oxford (~1889–1893). He co-founded the Numismatic Society of India and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1893 to 1927.

Indologist and historian Richard Carnac Temple studied at Harrow and Cambridge. He served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, edited the Indian Antiquary (~1885–1931), founded Panjab Notes and Queries (1883), and was an Honorary Fellow of Trinity Hall.

Linguist and Indologist Richard Constant Boer completed his Ph.D. at the University of Groningen in 1888, where he served as Privatdozent until 1900. From 1900 to 1929, he was Professor of Old Germanic and Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam.

Richard D. Mann, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, completed his Ph.D. at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003) and later held an appointment at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Richard D. McBride II, working in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned his Ph.D. from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held positions at Dongguk University and Brigham Young University, where he became Associate Professor of Asian and Near Eastern Languages.

Richard De Smet was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Robert Antoine and Michel Ledrus, completing his Ph.D. at the Pontifical Gregorian University in 1954. That year, he became Professor of Logic, Metaphysics, and Indian Philosophy at De Nobili College.

Archaeologist Richard Delbrück studied at Neuchâtel, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn (Ph.D. 1899). He directed the German Archaeological Institute in Rome (1911–1915) and held professorships in classical archaeology at Jena (~1911–1928), Giessen (1922–1928), and Bonn (1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his AM and PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at Saint Xavier, SAIC, and Wisconsin-Madison, and was Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University Bloomington (2013–2021).

Indologist Richard Fick earned his Ph.D. at Kiel University under Richard Pischel and Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Kiel University Library and the Prussian State Library, became director of the Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932), and was Honorary Professor at Göttingen.

id: P:Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John
summary: Richard Fleming St. Andrew St. John was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Wadham College, Oxford (M.A.). He taught Burmese at University College London in 1894 and served as Teacher of Hindūstânî at Oxford from 1890 to 1910.

Richard Foltz is an Iranian and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Utah and Harvard. He taught at Kuwait, Brown, Columbia, and Florida before joining Concordia University in 2005, serving as founding director of its Centre for Iranian Studies.
Richard Francis Burton was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Trinity College, Oxford, beginning in 1840, and later founded the Kama Shastra Society.

Indologist Richard Fritzsche earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig (~1869–1873), studying under Hermann Brockhaus, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and Georg Curtius. He taught at Königliches Gymnasium Chemnitz (1876–1888) and served as Rektor of Gymnasium Schneeberg (~1894–1918).

Richard G. Salomon, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studied under Ludo Rocher. He became a professor at the University of Washington around 1981, eventually serving as Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit.
